office_does: The Clark County Council adopts the county budget and property-tax levies, sets councilmanic taxes and fees, adopts the growth-management comprehensive plan and land-use rules for unincorporated areas, and decides which county propositions go to voters.
race_blurb: Incumbent Michelle Belkot, who cast the lone votes against the 2026 levy increase and the housing sales tax, faces teacher John Zingale, who says the county should use its allowed 1% levy increase and invest in roads, parks, housing and social services.

candidates.summary: First-term District 2 councilor, a military veteran and former federal procurement official who runs on no new taxes, opposition to annexation and light-rail tolls, and law-enforcement funding.
highlights: Only council vote against the 1% general-fund levy increase in the 2026 budget [S4]
Lone vote against the 0.1% housing sales tax, citing no spending plan [S5]
Prioritizes law enforcement, fire and infrastructure "before expanding programs or increasing spending" [S1]
Opposes light-rail taxes and tolls and Vancouver annexation of District 2 [S2]
Moved the resolution placing the Proposition 12 jail bond on the ballot [S6]

taxes.basis: Recorded no votes on the 2026 levy increase and the housing sales tax, and a "No New Taxes" platform.

spending.basis: Core services before program growth and demands a tracking and spending plan before new revenue, while backing public-safety funding.

housing.basis: Opposes impact fees and new development fees and voted against the housing sales tax, though she voted to extend the mobile-home-park moratorium.

safety.basis: Repeatedly puts law-enforcement funding first and says she stands with local, state and federal law enforcement.

experience.basis: First-term incumbent in office since 2023 running on her council record.

candidates.summary: Middle-school history teacher, 2026 Southwest Washington Teacher of the Year and teachers' union representative, running for office for the first time.
highlights: Says skipping the allowed 1% property-tax increase contributed to the deficit and "we do need to find ways to increase revenue" [S3]
Names roads, parks, public safety and housing as spending priorities and would explore a metropolitan park district [S3]
Favors building "up, not out" with a mix of housing sizes [S3]
Endorsed by Councilors Sue Marshall and Wil Fuentes, Sen. Adrian Cortes and Vancouver Mayor Anne McEnerny-Ogle [S4]

taxes.basis: Supports using the 1% annual levy increase and finding new revenue to avoid service cuts.

spending.basis: Calls for investing in social services, infrastructure and parks and warns budget cuts threaten essential services.

safety.basis: Wants a holistic, affordability-centered approach to homelessness and more behavioral-health capacity rather than a drug-use framing.

experience.basis: First-time candidate with no elected public office; teacher and union representative.
